chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Hassaan, from Abu Ali who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: Do not mention our secrets in opposition to our public statements, and do not mention our public statements in opposition to our secrets. It suffices for you that you say what we say, and remain silent about what we remain silent about. Indeed, you have seen that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has not made any good for anyone of the people in opposition to us.
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'So let those beware who go against his order lest a trial afflict them or there befalls upon them a painful chastisement.'
ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between the Imams' private secrets and public statements according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of 'Taqiyya' (dissimulation) and the strategic alignment of the Imams' public and private teachings, instructing followers to mirror the Imam's speech and silence to maintain doctrinal consistency. It underscores the theological authority of the Ahl al-Bayt, asserting that divine favor is exclusive to their followers, while deviation invites 'fitna' (trial) or 'adhab alim' (painful punishment). This guidance reflects the historical context of navigating political and social pressures while preserving the core esoteric truths of the Imamate.
